questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Match the following TFT indications to the source's classification — 1) Universal neonatal screen 2) Routine community screening in adults 3) High-yield targeted screen … A) All newborns B) Not recommended routinely C) Symptomatic / high-risk groups
questions.exp: The page recommends universal neonatal screening, advises against routine adult screening, and reserves tests for symptomatic or at-risk groups. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: A healthy 30-year-old has a free-T4 normal but total T4 elevated. Pregnancy is excluded and she is on combined oral contraceptive pills. The most consistent pattern is:
opts: Low TBG with normal free T4
Increased TBG with normal free hormone
Increased TSH with low free T4
questions.exp: OCPs raise TBG; total T4/T3 rise with free hormone and TSH normal. This must be distinguished from the rare FDHS where albumin binds excess T4. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Assess these TBG-effect statements: I Estrogen, pregnancy and chronic active hepatitis raise TBG. II Nephrotic syndrome lowers TBG.
questions.exp: OCPs, estrogen, pregnancy, steroid therapy and chronic active hepatitis raise TBG; nephrotic syndrome, androgen and chronic liver disease lower TBG. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Match the following TBG change to its source — 1) ↑TBG 2) ↓TBG … A) Nephrotic syndrome B) Combined oral contraceptive pill
questions.exp: The source lists OCPs, pregnancy, steroids and chronic active hepatitis under TBG excess, and nephrotic syndrome with protein-losing states under TBG deficit. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: A patient on chronic glucocorticoids for SLE has normal free T4 and TSH, but total T4 is high. The biochemical mechanism is:
opts: Antibody-bound T4 with low free hormone
questions.exp: Corticosteroids raise TBG and therefore raise total T4/T3 while free hormones and TSH remain normal. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Which condition is the odd one out compared with the others as a cause of raised TBG on this page?
questions.exp: Nephrotic syndrome lowers TBG; estrogen, pregnancy and chronic active hepatitis all raise TBG per the source. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: The most abundant thyroid-hormone transport protein on this page is ___, binding approximately two-thirds of circulating T4.
questions.exp: TBG carries the largest fraction of T4 and T3; prealbumin and albumin bind smaller portions. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Evaluate these source statements on neonatal screening: I It is universally recommended for all newborns. II It targets congenital hypothyroidism to prevent cretinism.
questions.exp: Universal newborn screening is standard practice because early levothyroxine prevents neurodevelopmental cretinism. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Match the following drugs / states to their TBG effect — 1) Androgen 2) Chronic liver disease 3) Oestrogen therapy 4) Nephrotic syndrome … A) ↑TBG B) ↓TBG
questions.exp: Androgen, chronic liver disease and nephrotic syndrome all lower TBG; only oestrogen therapy raises it. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: A laboratory reports normal free T4 with high total T4 in a clinically euthyroid patient on OCPs. What is the correct clinical action?
opts: No treatment — interpret total T4 in light of TBG change
Start levothyroxine because total T4 is high
Start methimazole because total T4 is high
Repeat total T4 only after stopping OCPs
questions.exp: Free hormone and TSH are normal; the high total T4 reflects raised TBG from estrogen, not true hyperthyroidism. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Per the source, the binding protein transporting the largest fraction of circulating thyroid hormone is:
questions.exp: TBG carries the majority of T4 and T3; prealbumin and albumin take much smaller fractions. (Book p902)

questions.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
questions.q: Assess the printed TBG list: I The source inherits (rare) as a TBG-excess cause. II Inherited deficiency is listed separately from nephrotic syndrome.
questions.exp: The page lists inherited (rare) as a separate TBG-excess cause and inherited deficiency as a separate TBG-deficit cause from acquired nephrotic losses. (Book p902)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Match the listed pituitary/hypothalamic feedback states to their typical free-hormone / TSH pattern — 1) Primary thyrotoxicosis 2) Sick-euthyroid (printed pattern) 3) Resistance to thyroid hormone (RTH) … A) ↑FT4, ↓TSH B) Normal FT4, normal TSH (printed totals look low) C) Normal/slightly raised FT4 with normal/raised TSH
questions.exp: Primary thyrotoxicosis raises free T4/T3 and suppresses TSH; sick-euthyroid as printed leaves totals normal with rT3 high and free T3 low; RTH is associated with normal/raised free hormones and non-suppressed TSH. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: An ICU patient has normal TSH, low total T3 and elevated rT3 one week after admission for sepsis. The most consistent interpretation is:
questions.exp: Low T3 with high rT3 in critical illness fits the source's sick-euthyroid sequence; primary hypothyroidism would also raise TSH. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Assess these sick-euthyroid statements per the source: I T4 is normal in the early phase. II Reverse T3 typically rises because D3 activity dominates.
questions.exp: The page prints T4 as normal with T3 low and reverse T3 high early in non-thyroidal illness. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Which condition is the odd one out among the source's TSH-suppressed (primary thyrotoxicosis) mimics?
questions.exp: RTH typically has non-suppressed TSH because the pituitary resists thyroid hormone feedback, unlike primary thyrotoxicosis where TSH is suppressed. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: In sick-euthyroid syndrome, the source lists elevated ___ as the most characteristic biochemical marker.
questions.exp: Reverse T3 rises because deiodinase type-3 inactivates T4 to rT3 instead of activating it to T3. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: A patient has persistently non-suppressed TSH with raised free T4 and a normal alpha-subunit / pituitary MRI. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Non-suppressed TSH with raised free hormone and a normal MRI in a familial setting fits RTH; TSHoma typically raises the alpha-subunit and shows a sellar mass. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Match the following state to the expected TSH/free-T4 print on the page — 1) Primary thyrotoxicosis 2) Primary hypothyroidism 3) TSHoma 4) Sick-euthyroid early … A) ↑FT4, ↓TSH B) ↓FT4, ↑TSH C) ↑FT4, non-suppressed TSH D) Total T3 ↓, rT3 ↑, TSH normal
questions.exp: Primary thyrotoxicosis suppresses TSH; primary hypothyroidism raises TSH; TSHoma gives raised free hormone with non-suppressed TSH; early sick-euthyroid preserves total T4 with low T3 and high rT3. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Evaluate pituitary feedback: I RTH usually presents with low TSH and high free T4. II Sick-euthyroid syndrome typically produces normal TSH in its early stage.
questions.exp: RTH has non-suppressed TSH; sick-euthyroid typically keeps TSH normal early. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: After cardiopulmonary bypass a patient is clinically euthyroid but has total T3 below range, rT3 above range and normal TSH. Which intervention is most consistent with the source?
opts: No replacement — observe and treat the underlying illness
questions.exp: Sick-euthyroid changes are adaptive; the source does not recommend routine hormone replacement for ICU patients. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Which gene is the source's classic association with resistance to thyroid hormone?
questions.exp: RTH is most commonly linked to thyroid-hormone receptor β mutations on the page. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: In critical illness, the source's preferred test for diagnosing underlying thyroid disease is ___.
opts: Free T4 (and free T3) rather than total T4
questions.exp: Total T4 is misleading because TBG and albumin drop in critical illness; free hormone assays are the page's preferred test. (Book p903)

questions.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
questions.q: Which is the odd one out — a state where TSH typically rises (per the source's grouping)?
questions.exp: Early sick-euthyroid syndrome keeps TSH normal, whereas primary hypothyroidism, recovery from thyroiditis and iodine deficiency all can elevate TSH. (Book p903)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Match the printed biochemical pattern — 1) Thyrotoxicosis 2) T3-toxicosis 3) Sick-euthyroid (page schematic) 4) ↓TBG (cirrhosis) … A) ↓TSH, normal T4, ↑FT4, normal T3, ↑FT3 B) ↓TSH, normal T4, normal FT4, normal T3, ↑FT3 C) Normal totals, ↑rT3, ↓FT3 D) Normal totals, ↓TBG
questions.exp: The schematic prints thyrotoxicosis as ↓TSH with normal T4 but raised FT4 and normal T3 with raised FT3; T3-toxicosis raises only FT3; sick-euthyroid leaves totals normal with rT3 high and FT3 low; cirrhosis drops TBG without changing free hormone. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: A patient has suppressed TSH with normal total T4 and total T3 but elevated free T3. The most consistent label is:
questions.exp: Isolated free-T3 elevation with otherwise normal totals fits the page's T3-toxicosis pattern. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Assess the source's totals/free schematic: I Thyrotoxicosis row shows FT4 and FT3 both elevated. II Sick-euthyroid row prints normal total hormone values.
questions.exp: The thyrotoxicosis row has both FT4 and FT3 raised; the sick-euthyroid row keeps totals normal with FT3 low. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Match the following state to its TBG / binding-protein print on the page — 1) Pregnancy 2) Cirrhosis 3) Familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia … A) ↑TBG B) ↓TBG C) Albumin binds excess T4, raising total T4 with normal free hormone
questions.exp: Pregnancy raises TBG; cirrhosis lowers TBG; FDHS binds excess T4 to albumin raising total T4 with normal free hormone. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: A patient with cirrhosis has normal free T4, normal TSH, low TBG and low total T4. The free-hormone result correctly classifies the patient as:
questions.exp: Cirrhosis lowers TBG and therefore total T4, but free T4 and TSH are preserved — the patient is euthyroid. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Thyroglobulin is ___ in every cause of hyperthyroidism except ___, where it is low.
questions.exp: The page lists thyroglobulin as raised in all causes of thyrotoxicosis except factitious ingestion, where it is low. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Assess the source's thyroglobulin teaching: I Thyroglobulin is raised in subacute thyroiditis. II Thyroglobulin is raised in factitious thyrotoxicosis.
questions.exp: Subacute thyroiditis releases stored thyroglobulin, raising it; factitious intake of exogenous hormone suppresses thyroid activity so thyroglobulin is low. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Match the following pattern to the expected free hormone on the page — 1) Subclinical hyperthyroidism 2) T3-toxicosis 3) FDHS 4) Factitious thyrotoxicosis … A) Normal FT4, normal FT3, ↓TSH B) Normal FT4, ↑FT3, ↓TSH C) ↑Total T4, normal free hormone, normal TSH D) ↑FT4, ↓TSH, low thyroglobulin
questions.exp: Subclinical hyperthyroidism has normal free hormones with low TSH; T3-toxicosis raises only free T3; FDHS raises only total T4; factitious raises free T4 with low thyroglobulin. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: An over-the-counter 'thyroid support' user has suppressed TSH, raised free T4 and a low thyroglobulin. Which diagnostic label fits?
questions.exp: Factitious intake suppresses endogenous thyroid activity and therefore thyroglobulin, while exogenous T4 raises free T4. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Which is the odd one out — a state where thyroglobulin is raised?
questions.exp: Factitious thyrotoxicosis is the only cause on the page where thyroglobulin is low; the others raise thyroglobulin. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: In the page's sick-euthyroid arrow schematic, which direction does the FT3 arrow point?
questions.exp: The schematic draws FT3 down as part of the low-T3 / high-rT3 pattern of non-thyroidal illness. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: In familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia, total T4 is ___ while free T4 and TSH remain ___.
questions.exp: Albumin-binding variants raise total T4 but free T4 and TSH are preserved; FDHS mimics true hyperthyroidism only on total assays. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Assess this sick-euthyroid note: I The schematic marks rT3 as up. II The schematic marks FT3 as up.
questions.exp: Reverse T3 is marked up while free T3 is marked down, reflecting impaired T4-to-T3 activation and dominant D3 in critical illness. (Book p904)

questions.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
questions.q: Match the following thyrotoxicosis pattern to its free-hormone print — 1) Graves disease 2) Subacute thyroiditis 3) Toxic adenoma 4) Struma ovarii … A) ↑FT4 and ↑FT3 B) ↑FT4 with low thyroglobulin only in factitious C) ↑FT4/FT3 from ectopic thyroid tissue D) Transient ↑FT4 with raised thyroglobulin and ESR
questions.exp: Graves and toxic adenoma raise both FT4 and FT3; subacute thyroiditis causes a transient rise with raised thyroglobulin and ESR; struma ovarii produces ectopic thyroid hormone secretion. (Book p904)

units.title: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects
units.sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects · p902
units.guide: Anchor the universal neonatal screen, the negative recommendation for routine community screening, and the binding-protein model. Distinguish true thyroid disease from TBG- and albumin-driven changes in total hormone so treatment is not triggered by estrogens, pregnancy, steroids or liver disease.

units.title: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states
units.sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states · p903
units.guide: Layer pituitary feedback on top of the binding-protein model. Connect low T3 / high rT3 to non-thyroidal illness and learn why RTH breaks the simple suppress-TSH-with-excess-hormone rule.

units.title: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin
units.sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin · p904
units.guide: Read the page's totals vs. frees table as a flowchart. Tie thyroglobulin behaviour to factitious versus endogenous thyrotoxicosis so thyroiditis, toxic nodules and surreptitious intake can be separated biochemically.
